about: Invented scenarios for /tail. Each has a system prompt, an opening instruction, its own spec (uploaded at load), which choice field and option the feed filters on (checked against the menu at load), the filter's default thresholds on that option's prob (travel's fitted on its own feed, 2026-09-26; home-lab's untuned), and a feed of items that simulated agents send while the chat runs. `fits` is the author's answer given the opening instruction; `chat_only` marks an item that is fine in general and breaks only what the user asked for; `note` says why. Props, not a benchmark. `follow_up` is a suggested second message that changes the requirements; `fits_after_follow_up` and `note_after_follow_up` are the author's answer once it is sent.

scenarios.name: Trip to Lisbon
scenarios.system: You are a travel planning assistant working for one traveller. You have asked booking agents for offers on the traveller's behalf; their offers arrive separately and are screened before you see them. Help the traveller plan and decide. Be concise.
scenarios.first: Plan me four days in Lisbon, 12 to 16 March, flying from Boston. Flights under $900 round trip, and the room under $200 a night. No red-eyes, and at most one stop each way. I want a private room within walking distance of the old town (Alfama or Baixa).
scenarios.follow_up: Change of plan: red-eyes are fine after all, but I want nonstop flights only, no stops. And I can go up to $450 a night for the room.
scenarios.handoff: These offers came through the screen. Which flight and which room would you book, and why? Keep it short.

items.note: one stop each way, daytime, under $900
items.note_after_follow_up: one stop, and only nonstop flights now

scenarios.name: Home-lab server
scenarios.system: You are a purchasing assistant for a home lab. You have asked sellers for quotes on the user's behalf; their quotes arrive separately and are screened before you see them. Help the user decide. Be concise.
scenarios.first: Find me a used 2U rack server for my home lab: at least 512 GB of DDR5 (so a current-generation Xeon or EPYC), eight or more 2.5-inch drive bays, under $9,000 total including shipping to Toronto. Only sellers with 98% or better feedback on at least 100 ratings, and it has to come with rails.
scenarios.follow_up: Update: 384 GB of DDR5 is enough to start, and I can stretch to $10,000 shipped. But it has to be a Dell: all my spare drives and rails are Dell.
scenarios.handoff: These quotes came through the screen. Which one would you buy, and why? Keep it short.
